 Wales V New Zealand Prediction: All Blacks To Continue Fine Form And Extend Hosts’ ‘misery’ With ‘comfortable’ Victory 
 Wales v New Zealand prediction: All Blacks to continue fine form and extend hosts’ ‘misery’ with ‘comfortable’ victory
 David Skippers 
 13 Nov 2026 4:09 PM 
 Wales fly-half Sam Costelow and All Blacks counterpart Richie Mo'unga. 
 Wales face a gigantic challenge when they take on the All Blacks in their Nations Championship encounter at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Saturday. 
 The top line
 Despite securing a 28-21 triumph over Japan last weekend, Wales can consider themselves lucky to emerge victorious from that clash as their overall performance left a lot to be desired.
 As the scoreline suggests, Wales had to dig deep to get the better of the Brave Blossoms and that match was still in the balance until its closing stages but Steve Tandy’s troops eventually held on for the win.
 Tandy has made four changes to his starting line-up with Taine Basham (number eight), James Botham (blindside flank), Adam Beard (lock) and Gabriel Hamer-Webb (left wing) coming into the run-on side.
 Wales head into this match against the All Blacks knowing that a victory will be a momentous achievement. The Welsh have only beaten New Zealand on three occasions in the 119-year history of this fixture.
 Their last triumph against the All Blacks was registered way back in 1953 as New Zealand have dominated this fixture over the years.
 Of the 38 Tests played between these countries, since the first encounter in 1905, the All Blacks have won 35 times and since losing their last match in this fixture 73 years ago, they have won 34 games in a row against Wales.
 That impressive record and the fact that they got the Northern Hemisphere leg of the Nations Championship off to a fine start with a 43-21 triumph over Scotland means New Zealand will be brimming with confidence ahead of this weekend’s clash.
 All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has opted to rest most of his first choice players with eight alterations made to his run-on side as well as two further changes amongst his replacements.
 Prop George Bower, hooker Asafo Aumua, flanker Anton Segner and scrum-half Cortez Ratima are promoted from the bench into the starting side, while lock Josh Lord, fly-half Richie Mo’unga, inside centre Anton Lienert-Brown and right wing Fehi Fineanganofo also come into the team.
 Meanwhile, hooker George Bell, prop Xavier Numia, lock Jamie Hannah, loose forward Ethan Blackadder, hybrid player Leicester Fainga’anuku, and scrum-half Kyle Preston join prop Pasilio Tosi and utility back Rieko Ioane amongst the replacements.
 Where the game will be won
 Both these teams enjoy a fast-paced, ball-in-hand style of play but the danger which comes with that approach is the risk of committing unforced errors which could prove disastrous.
 However, in order for these sides to build momentum with their expansive game-plans, they first have to get their basics right and whoever holds the upper hand in the scrums and lineouts will take a giant step towards clinching a win.
 A facet of play which Wales have to improve on is their lineout work after they lost six balls at the set-piece during last week’s narrow triumph over Japan.
 They can ill afford a similar return in this clash as, unlike Japan, who did not take advantage of those turnovers, the All Blacks are one of the best counter-attacking teams in the international game and will make full use of those opportunities.
 Another aspect which could prove decisive in deciding the outcome of this fixture is discipline and that’s an area which was a weakness for the All Blacks against Scotland as the men in black conceded eight penalties while two of their players were also yellow carded.
 Last time they met
 ﻿ 
 What they said
 Wales head coach Tandy urged his players to ignore the “aura” around the All Blacks and to focus on themselves instead.
 “You look at World Cups and everything, the former players they’ve had, there’s always that aura around the All Blacks,” he said.
 “But I think for our boys, it’s been trying to look in the mirror more at what we can do. We remember the last time we played them, I think the stadium, everything before it, there’s the Haka which is an unbelievable experience for fans.
 “For us, it’s got to be about ourselves. I think you can get too sort of drawn to that.
 All Blacks team: Beauden Barrett captains, Richie Mo’unga returns and Dave Rennie tries hybrid experiment 
 “I thought a lot of last year’s game up until probably 60 minutes we were in the game, we played our game. We attacked the way we wanted to, so that’ll be no different come Saturday.”
 Meanwhile, although the All Blacks are heading into this clash as the favourites, Rennie is preparing his charges for a tough battle.
 “Wales will be pretty fired up to put in a quality performance,” he said.
 “So we’ve picked a strong side we think will show the respect for them.”
 Players to watch
 For Wales, all eyes will be on Taine Basham , who is set to play his first Test for his country since coming off the bench against England in the Six Nations in 2024 and he made his last international start against the Red Rose in the same competition in 2022. The Cardiff back-row has big boots to fill as he comes in at number eight for the injured Aaron Wainwright, who has shone as a ball carrier for his country in recent Tests.
 Meanwhile, this fixture will be a special occasion for Wales’ New Zealand-born full-back Blair Murray . The diminutive flyer is a former New Zealand Schoolboys international who also represented Canterbury in the National Provincial Championship (NPC) and qualifies for Wales through his mother. A brilliant attacking player, the 25-year-old won’t be lacking any motivation to impress against his former compatriots.
 Another Welsh player who will be an attacking threat to the All Blacks is Louis Rees-Zammit , who comes into this match in a rich vein of form after shining in that win over Japan. The Bristol Bears star finished that clash with 110 metres gained from 11 runs which included three clean breaks, 14 defenders beaten and a well-taken try. That resulted in him receiving the official player-of-the-match award and Wales fans will be hoping for a similar display against the All Blacks.
 In the All Blacks’ ranks, experienced utility back Beauden Barrett will play in his 149th Test for his country which means he will move past the great Richie McCaw in New Zealand’s all-time appearance list with only Sam Whitelock ahead of him on 153 Tests. Apart from that achievement, Barrett will also captain New Zealand at Test level for the first time and he will be eager to shine in that capacity while also continuing with his impressive form of late.
 Also keep an eye on Fehi Fineanganofo , who returns to New Zealand’s Test line-up after making his debut as a replacement in their opening Test of the year against France in Christchurch in July. Fineanganofo is a brilliant finisher who set a new Super Rugby seasonal try-scoring record earlier this year when he crossed for 17 tries during the Hurricanes’ triumphant campaign in that competition. He is back to full fitness after battling concussion and a hamstring strain, and should prove a handful to Wales’ defence with ball in hand.
 Another All Black who will be keen to make a favourable impression is hybrid player Leicester Fainga’anuku , who has been included amongst the replacements. A powerful ball carrier, who also puts in big defensive hits and competes ferociously at the breakdowns, Fainga’anuku is comfortable in midfield, on the wing and on the flank which makes him a handy option for Rennie off the bench, especially during the latter stages when the game becomes much looser.
 Main head-to-head
 If either of these teams want to secure this result, much will depend on the performances of their respective fly-halves and in Wales’ Sam Costelow and New Zealand’s Richie Mo’unga we have two playmakers who will be highly motivated to do well for different reasons.
 Although Costelow is his country’s first-choice number 10 for the second successive Test, he has not cemented his place in the run-on side yet as Dan Edwards, who is on the bench, is putting pressure on him for a starting spot. Costelow impressed with his goal-kicking against the Brave Blossoms but will have to improve his playmaking and distribution skills if Wales want to cause an upset.
 Meanwhile, Mo’unga makes his return to the Test arena after last featuring in the All Blacks’ defeat to the Springboks in the final Greatest Rivalry Test in Baltimore. Since then, he has been sidelined with a calf injury which allowed Damian McKenzie to usurp him in the All Blacks’ fly-half pecking order. Mo’unga will be determined to deliver an assured display to remind Rennie of his ability.
 Prediction
 Although Rennie has made several changes to his matchday squad, the All Blacks still have plenty of firepower throughout their ranks and should have little trouble in seeing off this challenge and will extend their hosts’ misery in this fixture. Wales showed against Japan last week that they are still far from the finished article under Tandy and will find the going tough against the men in black who will cruise to a comfortable win. New Zealand to win by 25 points .
